summary:
Items 5, 6, and 7 give 3 open decisions and 2 closed things. I wrote drafts only, below /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/round7/decisions/documents-writes-rows. No file of the worktree changed, no GitHub write, no request to production.

Decisions (ids D-PRE-21 to D-PRE-23; D-PRE-24 to D-PRE-29 are not used):
- D-PRE-21: where the saved issue #1 text goes. Recommended: it moves with its folder, and contract line 7 keeps the link.
- D-PRE-22: the unused index of the task rows. Recommended: remove it with one new migration:
  `DROP INDEX work_tasks_review_queue;`  (27 rows become 24 for one decision, measured on a local D1; the removal writes 0 rows)
- D-PRE-23: the receipt of a webhook that starts no work. Recommended: no row. Example: one main commit of ariakit/ariakit had 33 check runs (measured with gh on 2026-10-07), which is 66 webhooks (assumption) and 264 written rows today; only 1 of the 66 can start work.

Closed, with no decision:
- operations/simplification-cutover.md: the question "Are the gates still in use?" is a fact, and the repository answers it. Each gate is complete (its lines 14, 26, 37, 55; docs/evidence/issue-204-completion.md:16-18; issue #204 is closed as completed). The file moves, and contract line 252 and README line 9 get new words.
- The row deletion of D-SCALE-03: the maintainer selected it in round 4 with its cost in the option text, and "3. Ok" plus the authorization close it. The test of carried approvals is a condition of the implementation and not a choice.

Verification: scripts/validate.mjs compares 74 quoted file:line facts with the repository (all equal) and checks the JSON form and the finding ids. The record build (build.mjs with --content and --out in my folder) accepts a copy of r7 with the 3 decisions and fragments: 61 decisions, no error. My own query plan check in SQLite 3.51.0 gives the same 5 plans with and without the index.

Important for the coordinator: the record's list of rules that D-SCALE-03 changes is not complete. S06 (contract line 137) and the saved issue #1 sentence "Preserve identity and acceptance history after byte expiry" (contract-issue-1.md:336) also change, and the contract pull request must replace them, or contract line 5 keeps them in force.

decisions.question: Where does the saved text of issue #1 go when the history moves to docs/history/?
decisions.options: (1) stay-in-docs: the file keeps its path docs/simplification-audit/contract-issue-1.md; docs/ then has each text in force, at about 2 times the words (5 files, 20,625 words after step 9); 16 lines in 5 moved files change. (2) move-with-folder: it moves with the 57 other files of its folder; contract line 7 keeps the link and "remains binding"; 3 lines change (contract 7 and 48, .gitattributes 5); 4 files with 10,385 words stay; docs/history/ then has one file in force. (3) end-binding: it moves, and contract line 7 says that it is no longer in force; each rule that must stay goes into the contract first; effort L, with a review of each rule.
decisions.recommended: move-with-folder. It is the count that D-CODE-04 already has, it changes 3 lines, and the rule that keeps the file in force is contract line 7 and not the folder. Wrong if the maintainer wants docs/ to hold each text in force (then option 1), or if the saved issue #1 text must no longer be in force (then option 3).
decisions.place: content/sections/45-code-ci-docs.html, part code-docs-volume, directly after the placeholder of D-CODE-04 and before the heading code-structure. New anchor: code-docs-issue-1. In decisions.json after D-CODE-04. Fragment: fragments/D-PRE-21.html.

decisions.question: Does the implementation remove the index work_tasks_review_queue, which no statement uses?
decisions.options: (1) keep-index: nothing changes; D14 is read as a rule for each object of the schema; each decision writes 3 rows more than it needs (27 for one variant, 46 for 4 variants). (2) drop-index: one new migration, DROP INDEX work_tasks_review_queue; 24 in place of 27 and 43 in place of 46 (measured, local D1); the removal writes 0 rows; no statement changes its plan; D14 is read as a rule for the retired backup and transfer tables only (contract lines 58 and 42).
decisions.recommended: drop-index. It removes 3 written rows from each decision, the removal writes nothing, and no statement uses the index. Wrong if the maintainer reads D14 as a rule for each schema object. The saving is small: 4,500 rows in 30 days at 50 decisions each day.
decisions.place: content/sections/40-data-storage.html, part data-scans, after the code block with statusRunEligibleSql and before the heading data-ancestry. New anchor: data-scans-old-index. In decisions.json after D-DATA-01. Fragment: fragments/D-PRE-22.html.

decisions.question: What does the service write to D1 for a GitHub webhook that starts no work?
decisions.options: (1) keep-receipts: a receipt for each webhook as today, 4 rows and 215 bytes each with no end; 264 rows for the example commit. (2) one-statement: one function says if an event has work; a webhook with no work gets one INSERT that is already processed: 2 rows in place of 4 (measured), 134 rows for the example commit; D1 keeps a row for each delivery. (3) no-receipt: the same function; a webhook with no work gets a log line and the 202, and no row: 4 rows for the example commit; the recovery needs no receipt for an answered delivery (github-deliveries.ts:236-239); D1 has no list of these deliveries.
decisions.recommended: no-receipt. It writes nothing for the webhooks that start no work (65 of 66 in the example), and no statement of the code lists or counts their rows. Wrong if the maintainer wants a D1 row for each delivery as an audit record (then option 2), or wants no function that sorts events before the receipt (then option 1). Money is small in each option: 0.61 USD each month at most in the estimate.
decisions.place: content/sections/40-data-storage.html, part data-retention, directly after the placeholder of D-DATA-04 and before the heading data-other. New anchor: data-retention-receipts. In decisions.json after D-DATA-04. Fragment: fragments/D-PRE-23.html.

closed: operations/simplification-cutover.md (second file of item 5). Not a choice: the question "Are the gates still in use?" is a fact that the repository gives (AUTHORING.md:463 forbids such a question). Evidence: the file says "Historical pending states below do not reopen completed or waived gates" (line 5), "authority receipts are complete" (line 14), "The linked completion record resolves them for the selected production rollout" (line 26), "Read their pending states and gates as historical evidence" (line 37), and "These commands do not run in the current checkout" (line 55). docs/evidence/issue-204-completion.md:16-18 has W06, W07, and W08 as "Complete in production". Issue #204 is closed as completed since 2026-10-02 (gh read). The 4 holds of its lines 28 to 31 each have a row in the contract (lines 47, 48, 51, 58). Words that close it: the note on D-CODE-04 "/docs/history keep in the same repo", and on 2026-10-07 "3. Ok" and "I authorize the implementation". The implementation must: move the file to docs/history/operations/ with the 15 other files; change contract line 252, which calls it "the current cutover guide", to point at the issue #204 map and at the dated record; remove "and removal gates" from README.md:9; change the path in .github/workflows/README.md:7 and apps/web/src/operations/README.md:32. The record states it in 15-your-answers.html, part your-answers-question-history (the second "Needs your word" item becomes a statement), and item 5 of the list keeps only contract-issue-1.md. Details: closed.md, part 1.

The row deletion of D-SCALE-03 (item 7). Not a choice: the maintainer selected the option in round 4, and its text named the cost ("the name of the reviewer of a single variant is lost", "An approval older than the window is not copied to a later run") and the checks that come first. The option that keeps the history (rows to R2) was offered and not selected. The test is a condition of the implementation; if a later run needs a row, the settled answer already says that the run "is not released". Words that close it: the round 4 selection, and on 2026-10-07 "3. Ok" and "I authorize the implementation, the GitHub writes, the two writes to production D1, and the package publication and the change in ariakit/ariakit." The contract pull request must add one row for D-SCALE-03 to a map of this audit that replaces 4 texts: D05 (contract line 50), the row "Closed history" (line 33), S06 (line 137), and contract-issue-1.md:336. Line 33 itself changes later, in the pull request that ships the deletion (contract line 42 permits a selected target before its code). Before the deletion code: the test of 5 readers (local-comparison.ts:21-37, 593, 612-637; baseline-promotion.ts:25-27; review-status.ts:25-35; closed-summary.ts:236-245), a definition of "a later run still needs", the delete order (reservations and replacements, then decisions, then comparison rows), the 3 counts in the run row, and new words for the 2 texts that promise a "permanent decision summary" (closed-summary.ts:17-18, review.ts:678). It comes back as a decision in one case only: the test shows that no rule keeps a review behavior of today for an open pull request (example: a second automatic approval after 30 days). The record states it in D-SCALE-03 (one more sentence in the rationale), in 40-data-storage.html note data-scale-checks, and item 7 goes out of the list. Details: closed.md, part 2.
wrongInRecord: 15-your-answers.html, part your-answers-d1-less, row 3: "You must say if such an event needs a receipt at all: the recovery reads the receipts." The reason is wrong. The recovery settles a delivery when a receipt exists OR when GitHub lists a status from 200 to 399 (apps/web/src/operations/github-deliveries.ts:236-239). So it needs no receipt for a webhook that got its 202.

40-data-storage.html, note data-scale-checks: the foreign keys to a decision row are in "migrations 0001 and 0024". Not complete. visonaut_decision_replacements has 2 more (apps/web/migrations/0006_acceptance.sql:2-3). No runtime code writes that table, and closed-summary.ts:244 reads it. Also each decision row points at its comparison row (0001_service.sql:141), so the decisions must be deleted first.

D-SCALE-03 rationale and item 9 of the list "What still needs your word": the list of changed rules is not complete. It names contract line 33, D05, and D-DATA-04. It does not name S06 (docs/current-contract.md:137; "S06 keeps a permanent compact decision and identity summary" in docs/simplification-audit/handoff-draft.md:21; line 130 keeps it binding) and the saved issue #1 sentence "Preserve identity and acceptance history after byte expiry" (contract-issue-1.md:336, binding by contract line 7). It also does not name 2 product texts that promise a "permanent decision summary" (apps/web/src/operations/closed-summary.ts:17-18, apps/web/src/api/review.ts:678).

15-your-answers.html, list item 6 and row 2 of the table of your-answers-d1-less: "It needs your word: an earlier decision of yours (D14) says 'No destructive migration'". Not exact. The D14 row is about "Applied backup and transfer tables" (docs/current-contract.md:58), and line 42 says "The replacement scope below is exact". No contract line forbids the removal of an index. D-PRE-22 asks it as a question about the scope of D14.

15-your-answers.html, part your-answers-question-history: "If the gates are still in use, that file stays." The file answers this itself: no gate is pending. The part also does not say that contract line 252 calls the file "the current cutover guide" and tells the reader to follow it, so that line needs new words and not only a new path.

Not wrong, but it can be exact: "24 in place of 27 for a decision, with both old indexes removed". The 3 rows all come from work_tasks_review_queue (results/review.txt: INSERT 5 to 4, two UPDATEs 4 to 3), because the second old index is on the receipt table, which a decision does not write.
doubts: The cutover file is closed and not a decision, but the task text expected two small choices for item 5. If the coordinator wants a panel: two options, "It moves" (recommended) and "It stays in docs/operations/", with the evidence of closed.md. The closure is wrong only if the maintainer plans one more removal under the exact conditions of lines 28 to 31 of the file; then those 4 list items go into the contract and the rest still moves.

D-PRE-23: the 2 webhooks for each check run are an assumption (from webhooks.ts:225-233, which reads check_run events of GitHub Actions, and from contract line 244). Nobody read the event subscriptions of the GitHub App or the webhook rate of production. One read-only statement makes it a fact and belongs to the authorized reads of item 3: SELECT event, COUNT(*), MIN(received_at) FROM github_webhook_delivery GROUP BY event. The 33 check runs are from one main commit (a7c8be2); a pull request commit can have another number.
D-PRE-23: I did not read how long GitHub keeps the delivery list of an App and how long Cloudflare keeps the Worker log. The option "No row" names both as limited (assumption).

D-PRE-22: the plan check ran in SQLite 3.51.0 on this computer and on a local D1 in round 1. Nobody ran it in production D1. The raw file of the 0 rows of DROP INDEX (check/results/ddl.txt) is not in the repository; only notes.md:54 of the round 2 research has the number.

D-PRE-22 is the smallest decision (4,500 rows in 30 days at 50 decisions each day). On a yes it can be one row of the fix list of D-DATA-01. The wider D14 question (the 11 tables and 1 view of finding D1-15, row 12 of the compatibility table, "Not free") is in none of the 11 items; D-PRE-22 does not ask it.

D-SCALE-03: the record does not define "a later run still needs". closed.md gives a definition from the code. visonaut_reservations.decision_id is NOT NULL with a foreign key (0001_service.sql:160), so a reservation goes with its decision or the run is not released. For the lineage main, these decision rows can stay with no end (one for each screenshot that was new or removed on main). Nobody ran the test.

D-SCALE-03: the scheduled step of the deployed code deletes the copies that exist in production. I read this as a part of "I authorize the implementation" and not as a third write to production D1. The coordinator can confirm.

D-SCALE-03: I read "3. Ok" so: the contract pull request records the selected rule in a map now, and contract line 33 changes later, with the code. If the coordinator wants line 33 changed in the first contract pull request, the contract then describes a behavior that the code does not have until step 2 of D-DATA-02.

Section 15 is in work for r8. The fragments go into sections 40 and 45 (section 15 has 0 decision placeholders in r7), but the links from section 15 name parts of r7: your-answers-question-history, your-answers-d1-less, your-answers-word.

D-PRE-21: the counts "5 files with 20,625 words" and "4 files with 10,385 words" are the state after step 9 of the order (adapter-service-pins.md is then history). Before step 9: 6 files with 22,482 words and 5 files with 12,242. The recommended option needs a README in docs/history/ that names the one file in force; that README does not exist and D-CODE-04 does not name it.
The trial build passed build.mjs on a copy of r7. I did not look at the panels in a browser, I did not run check.mjs, and I did not build on r8.
